title: The ferry back
logline: Tuesday. The ferry south. The suit in the back window again. The same kid — or another; the strip won't say — asks if it's a costume. Wood says it was.

panels.composition: The ferry's car deck, the Legacy, the suit in the back window. WOOD at the rail. The islands behind now. The mainland ahead.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, a ferry car deck with a faded green station wagon and a dark suit hanging in its rear window, a thin man at the rail, islands receding behind and a mainland ahead in bright light

panels.composition: A KID at the window, looking at the suit. The same kid? The strip draws him from behind.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, a child seen from behind looking at a suit in a car window while a thin man answers him
image.notes: Rhymes with dw_2014-07-15. Whether it's the same kid: reserved; from behind.

panels.composition: The sketchbook on the rail. The page: the Sound, two lines, and now a third — the wake.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, close-up of a sketchbook on a ferry rail with three ink lines on the page, a horizon, an island and a ferry's wake

panels.composition: The ferry from the water, going away, small. The wake. The light the same as a week ago. The strip is the same. Wood is not, and the strip does not say so.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, a ferry small on brilliant blue water heading away with a long white wake in blinding summer light, no words

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: 'It was.' The third line: the wake.
